+"""Reproduction: the RST reader/writer should accept ``header_rows``.
+
+The RST (simple reStructuredText table) reader/writer hardcodes a single
+name row (``SimpleRSTHeader.start_line = 1``,
+``SimpleRSTData.start_line = 3``) and ``RST.__init__`` does not accept a
+``header_rows`` keyword, unlike the ``fixed_width`` /
+``fixed_width_two_line`` readers which support ``header_rows`` (see
+astropy #13734).  A table with extra header rows (e.g. dtype/unit lines)
+cannot be read or written in the RST format.
+
+When the desired behavior is implemented this script should pass.
+Currently it fails with::
+
+    TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'header_rows'
+"""
+
+from io import StringIO
+
+from astropy.io import ascii
+
+# RST simple table with extra header rows: dtype, name, unit.
+table_in = (
+    "====   ======   =====\n"
+    "float  string   int\n"
+    "a      b        c\n"
+    "m      degrees  deg\n"
+    "====   ======   =====\n"
+    "1      hello    3\n"
+    "2      world    4\n"
+)
+
+header_rows = ["dtype", "name", "unit"]
+
+# 1) Reading: the RST reader should accept header_rows and pick up the
+#    extra header rows just like the fixed_width readers do.
+table = ascii.read(table_in, format="rst", header_rows=header_rows)
+assert list(table.colnames) == ["a", "b", "c"], table.colnames
+assert str(table["a"].info.dtype) == "float"
+assert str(table["b"].info.unit) == "degrees"
+assert list(table["a"]) == [1.0, 2.0]
+
+# 2) Writing: the RST writer should accept header_rows and emit the same
+#    rows in the same order.
+out = StringIO()
+ascii.write(table, out, format="rst", header_rows=header_rows)
+assert out.getvalue() == table_in, out.getvalue()
+
+print("SUCCESS: RST accepted header_rows for reading and writing")
